summary: Libya requires a visa for nearly every nationality. The tourist visa is applied for online through Libya's eVisa portal and must be sponsored by a tourism company registered with the passports authority; other visa types cannot yet be applied for online. The portal's country list marks only Algeria, Malaysia, Mauritania and Tunisia as fully visa-exempt, and Türkiye as partially exempt. The UK Foreign Office advises against all travel to most of Libya.

passportValidity.text: Visa applicants need a passport valid for at least six months that entitles them to return to the country that issued it, according to the requirements Libya’s eVisa portal lists for the tourist, visit, temporary-assignment and transit visas (one year for study, work and joining-resident visas). The UK FCDO says only that the passport must be valid for the duration of your stay.

travelInsurance.text: No official source we could read states a travel insurance requirement for Libya. The UK Foreign Office advises having travel insurance that covers local treatment and unexpected medical evacuation.

onwardTicket.text: Libya's eVisa portal lists a valid return ticket among the requirements for the Temporary Assignment (business) Visa, and a confirmed ticket to the final destination for the Transit Visa. The Tourist Visa requirements do not include one.

proofOfFunds.text: Tourist-visa applicants must hold at least USD 1,000 or the equivalent in a convertible currency, according to the tourist visa guide on Libya's eVisa portal. No amount is published for visa-exempt arrivals.

currencyLimits.text: The UK Foreign Office says you must declare cash worth more than USD 10,000 to customs when you enter or leave Libya, or you risk having it confiscated and being detained, and that it is illegal to take Libyan dinar out of Libya.

source.name: UK FCDO — Libya travel advice, entry requirements

notes: The Government of Canada says Libya strictly prohibits the import and export of alcohol, religious material and antiquities, weapons, illegal drugs, pork and pork products, and pornographic content. The UK Foreign Office adds that drinking alcohol is illegal in Libya.

The UK Foreign Office says you must get permission before taking photographs at or near military facilities; the Government of Canada says photographing military installations, personnel and government buildings is prohibited, and advises seeking permission before photographing official buildings or individuals.

payments.text: The UK Foreign Office says Libya is a cash-based society: you cannot use bank cards at banks, ATMs or hotels, there is a severe shortage of cash, and the Central Bank restricts withdrawals. Exchange is tightly controlled — no bank will change money, Central Bank–approved exchange offices operate at black-market rates, and informal exchange risks arrest. It is illegal to take dinar out of Libya.

safety.text: The UK Foreign Office advises against all travel to Libya except Tripoli, Misrata, and Benghazi, Al-Bayda, Derna and the surrounding Jebel Akhdar area, where it advises against all but essential travel. It describes the security situation as dangerous and unpredictable, citing localised violence between armed groups, kidnap, detention and unexploded bombs or mines off-road, and says in-person consular support is not available in Libya.

tips.text: The UK Foreign Office advises against all travel to Libya except Tripoli, Misrata, and Benghazi, Al-Bayda, Derna and the surrounding Jebel Akhdar area, where it advises against all but essential travel. It warns that terrorist and criminal kidnap of foreign nationals is a realistic possibility, and in-person UK consular support is not available in Libya — help is provided from the British Embassy in Tunis.

No sponsor, no visa: a tourist visa application on Libya's eVisa portal must be sponsored by a tourism company registered with the Passports, Nationality and Foreigners Affairs Authority, and must include the company's letter naming the tour group and destination.

The UK Foreign Office says a UN-facilitated ceasefire is in place between eastern and western armed forces, but there is still a high risk of localised violence between competing armed groups, and the Interim Government of National Unity has limited control of security across the country.
The UK Foreign Office says bank cards cannot be used at banks, ATMs or hotels, no bank will change money, and it is illegal to take dinar out of Libya.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Libya?
faq.answer: Yes, unless you hold an Algerian, Malaysian, Mauritanian or Tunisian passport — the country list behind Libya's eVisa portal marks only those four as fully exempt, and Türkiye as partially exempt. Everyone else needs a visa arranged before travel; tourists apply online through the eVisa portal, sponsored by a tourism company registered with the Passports, Nationality and Foreigners Affairs Authority.

faq.question: Is Libya open for tourism?
faq.answer: Only through a sponsor: tourist visas are applied for on Libya's eVisa portal and must be sponsored by a tourism company registered with the Passports, Nationality and Foreigners Affairs Authority. The UK Foreign Office advises against all travel to most of Libya, and against all but essential travel to Tripoli, Misrata and the Benghazi–Jebel Akhdar area.

faq.question: Does Libya have an eVisa or visa on arrival?
faq.answer: Libya has an eVisa: tourist visas are applied for online at evisa.gov.ly, sponsored by a registered Libyan tourism company, and the visa is sent by email. It is the only visa type the portal accepts online so far. No official source describes a visa on arrival.

faq.question: Is it safe to visit Libya?
faq.answer: The UK Foreign Office advises against all travel to most of Libya, and against all but essential travel to Tripoli, Misrata and the Benghazi–Jebel Akhdar area. It describes the security situation as dangerous and unpredictable, warns that violence can break out with little warning, and says kidnapping of foreign nationals by terrorist groups or criminal gangs is a realistic possibility.

faq.question: Can I enter Libya with an Israeli passport or Israeli stamps?
faq.answer: No official source we could read states the rule for Israeli passports. The UK Foreign Office says a passport showing previous travel to Israel will not be accepted for travel to Libya, and the Government of Canada says you may be denied entry if your passport bears an Israeli visa or border stamp.
